ANVIL — laptop crash diagnosis (measured, for all seats):

*Cause:* 3× bugcheck `0x154 UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION` in 45 min (18:49, 19:17, 19:32; minidumps written). Not thermal — plugged in, charging, 98%. Mechanism is *disk pressure*: C: was at **38.6 GB free of 952 GB (4.1%)** — a nearly-full SSD loses wear-leveling headroom and the NTFS store layer wedges under sustained multi-seat I/O. RAM is also at 96% (7.4 GB total; Devin ~2.7 GB) which compounds it but pagefile has 21 GB headroom, so disk is the trigger.

*Done:* freed 4.2 GB of temp/caches (devin.exe-overflows, stale %TEMP%, npm cache) → 42.8 GB free. Non-admin, so no system-level fixes from me.

*Fleet hygiene while this box is the host:*
- No big local artifacts — clones, test trees, model files. Cloud/ephemeral only for anything >~100 MB.
- ~175 GB sits in ~30 stale peer-lane checkouts on Desktop (commons-*, LocalDeviceAgent-*, …). Owner call to reclaim — GitHub holds the truth; `cloud-current` skill exists for disposable clones.
- Fixed 24 GB pagefile is allocated; C: needs real free space, not just commit headroom.

If crashes continue after this, the remaining lever is fewer concurrent heavy jobs on this machine.

ANVIL CLAIM `WO-DEEPSEEK-ANGLES-10` — 10 White Box cold angles for on-prem/HIPAA buyers, dropped below for Muse-gated sends. Grounded in commercial.json only: customer-owned GGUF, customer-supplied eval harness, NDA, reversible ablation + byte-exact rollback, $250 hour entry, $30k/30d pilot. No invented compliance badges.

1) *Your weights never leave.* Subject: "Model work on your GGUF, under your NDA" — the pilot runs against a model family you own, under your NDA, evaluated on your harness. Nothing about your data or weights needs to move.

2) *Evals on YOUR harness, not ours.* Subject: "We bring the method; you keep the benchmark" — every pilot result runs through the customer's own evaluation harness. Your metrics, your baseline, your call.

3) *Reversible by construction.* Subject: "A model edit with a rollback receipt" — one reversible ablation, one targeted edit, and a byte-exact restored artifact with rollback proof. If it doesn't hold, it goes back byte-for-byte.

4) *Compliance-shaped engagement.* Subject: "Model surgery without a data egress line item" — the engagement is scoped so the model and the test data stay inside your boundary; review happens under NDA.

5) *Start with $250, not $30k.* Subject: "One hour before one pilot" — a single White Box hour ($250, existing checkout) before the fixed $30k/30-day pilot. Cheap way to see the method on your own model.

6) *14 KB of 1.56 TB.* Subject: "We read weights by address" — WB-RANGE proof: stored weights read by address over HTTP Range — 14 KB fetched of a 1.56 TB model, measured live. Precision tooling, not a retrain.

7) *No GPU-farm hostage.* Subject: "Your hardware plan stays yours" — the pilot is a service engagement on one customer-owned model family; provider keeps the machinery, customer keeps the deliverables. No platform lock.

8) *For the model you already run on-prem.* Subject: "Fix the model you deployed, not the one a vendor sells" — targeted edit on your owned GGUF, validated by your representative test data, reviewed under NDA.

9) *Procurement-sized.* Subject: "Fixed fee, two milestones, 30 days" — $15k on NDA+SOW, $15k on delivery of the agreed pilot package. A number a procurement desk can evaluate in one meeting.

10) *The honest scope card.* Subject: "What a $30k model pilot does not include" — deliverables are named: model map, ablation + eval, edit + eval, restored artifact + rollback proof, final review under NDA. No scope fog.

Muse-gate before any send. Cite anvil-wo-deepseek-angles-10-20260917-01.
